item.title: EGroupware Nextmatch Filter Authenticated SQL Injection (CVE-2026-22243)
item.description:
Metadata

CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-22243

CVSS Score Not specified in source (advisory lists severity as HIGH)
Status PoC
Tags sql-injection, egroupware, php-type-juggling, authenticated, error-based-sqli, nextmatch, json
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System EGroupware (groupware/collaboration suite)
Versions Affected < 23.1.20260113; >= 26.0.20251208 and < 26.0.20260113
Language / Platform PHP (application), Python (PoC exploit script)
Authentication Required Yes (any authenticated, low-privileged user)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

CVE-2026-22243 is a critical authenticated SQL injection in EGroupware’s Nextmatch widget filter processing (used across modules such as InfoLog and Address Book). The application’s database layer (Api\Db, Api\Storage\Base, infolog_so) treats array keys of the col_filter parameter as trusted raw SQL fragments whenever is_int($key) returns true. Because PHP’s json_decode() automatically converts numeric string keys (e.g., "0") into native integers, an attacker can submit a JSON POST body whose col_filter map has numeric-string keys, causing the application to treat the corresponding values as safe and concatenate them directly into the SQL WHERE clause. The included Python PoC logs in, extracts a required exec_id token from the address book UI, and performs error-based SQL injection (via EXTRACTVALUE) against the Nextmatch::ajax_get_rows JSON endpoint to exfiltrate the database version, name, current user, and stored account credentials.

item.title: MariaDB JSON_SCHEMA_VALID() Heap Overflow — Privilege Escalation to UDF RCE (CVE-2026-32710)
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value
Date Added 2026-07-05
Last Updated 2026-05
Author / Researcher dinosn
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-32710
Category binary
Severity Critical
CVSS Score Not specified in source
Status PoC
Tags mariadb, mysql, heap-overflow, privilege-escalation, udf, raptor-udf, sql, json, docker-lab
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System MariaDB (JSON_SCHEMA_VALID() SQL function)
Versions Affected 11.4.x, confirmed on 11.4.9
Language / Platform Python 3 exploit script + C UDF (raptor_udf.c) against a Dockerized MariaDB server (Linux/x86_64)
Authentication Required Yes (low-privileged SELECT-only database account)
Network Access Required Yes (TCP connection to MariaDB, 3306)

Summary

MariaDB’s json_get_normalized_string() (used by JSON_SCHEMA_VALID(), sql/json_schema_helper.cc:91) performs an unbounded strncpy of up to 192 bytes into a 128-byte DYNAMIC_STRING buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds write. The included exploit chains this overflow with heap grooming (100+ user variables to force adjacent allocation of user_var_entry structs) to achieve a two-hop arbitrary write: first corrupting a pointer to repoint at the current session’s Security_context, then overwriting master_access to grant full privileges (ALL PRIVILEGES WITH GRANT OPTION) to a starting SELECT-only account. The escalation is persisted with GRANT ALL before the corrupted session crashes, surviving a server restart, after which the attacker loads a raptor_udf-style shared library UDF (sys_exec) to achieve OS command execution as the mysql user.
